thread.title: Close Update: Inflation Fears Fail to Dent Wall Street's Euphoria

title: Close Update: Inflation Fears Fail to Dent Wall Street's Euphoria
text:
Close Update: Inflation Fears Fail to Dent Wall Street's Euphoria February 15, 2018, 04:36:57 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo 
Wall Street's major market averages closed higher for a fifth straight day as investors dismissed strong inflation data and remained focused on the consistent gains in the technology and industrial sector with blue chips Boeing ( BA ), Apple ( AAPL ) and Cisco ( CSCO ) all closing with outsized gains. 
After pulling back from the opening highs on the combination of technical resistance at the 50-day moving average with soft factory output data, the Dow moved steadily higher throughout the day, regaining the 25,000 handle mid-afternoon. The Nasdaq outperformed culminating in its best 5-day rally in more than six years. 
The trade higher was aided by the 10-year Treasury note steering clear of the 3.0% yield and the volatility index staying below 20 for most of the day. 
Before the open, stocks were gaining ground from Wednesday's post-CPI rally, ignoring another set of hot inflation numbers that were recently blamed for last week's panic selling on Wall Street. 
The better-than-expected PPI was accompanied by a 7,000 gain in jobless claims and mixed manufacturing data from the NY and Philadelphia Fed. 
Just before the open, industrial production showed a 0.1% drop in January, below expectations for an increase of 0.3%. Additionally, December's healthy 0.9% gain was more than cut in half, and capacity utilization slowed for the first time in five months. Stocks retreated, luring in bargain-hunters, predominately in healthcare and tech stocks and later permeating all sectors of the S&P 500 with the exception of the energy sector. 
For Friday, the economic calendar includes January housing starts, January import and export prices and the preliminary February Univ of MI consumer sentiment index. 
On the earnings front, Campbell Soup ( CPB ), Coca-Cola ( KO ), Deere (DE) and Kraft Heinz (KHC) all report before Friday's open.
